subject: Using dBref in meanpec and spec

messages.author: e6ffb56610bd05a9
messages.subject: Using dBref in meanpec and spec
parts:
Greetings!
I am using your great package to look at the self noise of an accelerometer and have run into a problem.   Specificallly when I execute

meanspec(raw_data$Ax, f=(f*1000), wl=win_len, dB="max0", dBref=(sens*bw_sqrt) , flab="Frequency(Hz)", alab="Noise dBuG/Hz^0.5")

I get results that are not consistent.  I reviewd the source code in seewave.r and found that the spectral result is being normalized to the max bin
e.g. y3<-y2/max(y2)

If something like
if(is.null(dBref)) y3<-y2/max(y2)
else y3<-y2
were to be implemented when using dBref, then absolute calibrations could be performed. 

I edited the source code to try this out, but then my inexperience with building packages stopped me.  When I tried to execute
R CMD build seewave

the following error occurred
Error: processing vignette ‘seewave_IO.rnw’ failed with diagnostics:
 chunk 14
Error in library(sound) : there is no package called ‘sound’

How do I go about getting a changes like this implemented (locally and in the main branch)? 

Thanks
Mike

else y3<-y2
were to be implemented when using dBref, then absolute calibrations could be performed. 

I edited the source code to try this out, but then my inexperience with building packages stopped me.  When I tried to execute
R CMD build seewave

the following error occurred
Error: processing vignette ‘seewave_IO.rnw’ failed with diagnostics:
 chunk 14

So I fixed my petty compile problems by installing the package sound (appears to only be required for compile?).  And made the above modifications.  I also ran into an issue with the stft function when norm is set to false, the function still normalized the return values, I replaced the offending function with a window length normalization
#  else {z<-z2/max(z2)}
  else {z<-z2/(wl/2)}
which provides the expected response.
Cheers
Mike
